description: Digital Twin Builder (preview, Real-Time Intelligence) creates digital representations of real-world environments by modeling an ontology (namespaces, entity types, properties, relationship types) and mapping source data to entity instances. The ontology/instance data is stored in an auto-provisioned Fabric lakehouse named '<item-name>dtdm' and queried via that lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint. Modeling/mapping/contextualization are portal-only (no public REST API); the REST surface is item CRUD + definition only.

definition_parts.description: Single JSON part: {"LakehouseId": "<uuid>"} linking the DTB to its auto-provisioned '<name>dtdm' data lakehouse.

flags.--name: Display name (must start with a letter; letters, numbers, underscores only — NO hyphens; < 90 chars)

notes: Item name allows only letters, numbers, and underscores — hyphens are NOT allowed (unlike most item types).
create / getDefinition / updateDefinition are long-running (LRO) operations (~60-100s).
A '<name>dtdm' lakehouse is auto-created and linked (LakehouseId in the definition). Its SQL endpoint exposes the base layer (dbo Tables) and the domain layer (dom Views, recommended for querying).

The twin's DATA is queryable with T-SQL: use 'fabio digital-twin-builder query --id <DTB> --sql "SELECT * FROM dom.<View>"' (fabio resolves the dtdm lakehouse automatically), or 'fabio digital-twin-builder show-lakehouse --id <DTB>' to get the SQL endpoint.
Deleting the DTB does NOT delete the '<name>dtdm' lakehouse automatically — use 'fabio digital-twin-builder delete --id <DTB> --delete-lakehouse' to cascade.

Ontology modeling, data mapping, contextualization (relationships), and the Explorer are low-code/no-code PORTAL experiences with no public REST API; the definition.json blob is authored by the portal.
Flows (child items) execute the mapping/contextualization operations; see the DigitalTwinBuilderFlow schema. Flow execution is portal-driven (Run button / schedule).
related_commands: fabio digital-twin-builder query --workspace <WS> --id <ID> --sql "SELECT TOP 100 * FROM dom.<View>"
